newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegrin port sets up direct route to China.
newsitem.headline: Montenegrin port sets up direct route to China.

text.p: Montenegrin Adriatic port Luka Bar opened a direct shipping line with China to service domestic firms exporting goods under a Yugoslav-Chinese barter deal, a port representative said on Tuesday.
"The line will operate in five to seven week intervals at first but can increase in frequency according to client's needs," port spokeswoman Irina Dabovic told Reuters.
The first ship, a 15,000-tonne vessel operated by the China-Pol Broker shipping company based in Gdynia, Poland, left for China on Monday, she said.
Under the barter deal signed in March last year, China will export two million tonnes of crude oil in exchange for Yugoslav industry products.
The deal, initially signed for a year, was extended for five years at a Yugoslav-Chinese inter-government commission meeting in March 1997.
Machine factory 14. Oktobar of Krusevac and Belgrade motor and tractor factory Industrija motora i traktora (IMT) were the first firms to ship their products to China on the new route, Dabovic said.
Yugoslav firms had hitherto used the Black Sea ports of Constanta and Burgas and the Greek port of Salonika to ship their goods.
"We expect Yugoslav firms will turn to the port of Bar because it has the most attractive conditions," Dabovic said but gave no details.
